title: Press Play On Tape - Cassette Deck & VHS Packaging Interface

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: Cassette lined up side by side forming striped spool motifs; VHS packaging with ergonomic cut corners; A/B side flipping; magnetic tape movement; worn-out tapes jamming.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Services section arranged as cassettes side-by-side; graphic stripes animate through page layouts and titles mimicking tape travel; mechanical A/B-side flip animations with mechanical sound effects; 404 page is a worn-out jammed cassette rendered with WebGL shaders.

design_tokens.borders: Hard-edged cassette-window frames and packaging-cut corner silhouettes; stripes as full-bleed color bands, no rounded corners
design_tokens.elevation: Flat with 2D mechanical movement; depth from overlapping tape stripes and label layers, no drop shadows
design_tokens.typography: Bold uppercase sans-serif echoing VHS cover titles; category acronyms (VM, AB, S, SD) echoing cassette mode labels; filled 'O' glyphs animate as reactive sound circles

interactive_mechanics: Audio-reactive typography: Web Audio API listens to five frequency bands and scales the filled 'O' glyphs in real time
A/B side flip animations with mechanical cassette sounds on section transitions
Infinite scroll illusion: identical component at page start/end matching scale and color state for seamless loop
WebGL (Curtains.js) shader plane for the worn-tape 404 page
usability_notes: Every interaction emits sound, so audio must be opt-in and fully muteable (accessibility + autoplay policy). Best for audio/sound studios where audio-reactivity is the brand. Rainbow-stripe palette and mechanical animations can overwhelm; content hierarchy depends on restraining stripes to structural bands. Strong delight and memorability; heavier CPU/GPU cost on low-end devices.
